title: Is an Electron a Wave? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A light microscope cannot show you a single virus, but an electron microscope can. Ripples bend around a stone, yet a cricket ball never does. The answer to both puzzles is that every moving particle carries a wave. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we follow Aarav's question into the de Broglie relation.

On the molecule bench, an electron moves with its matter wave. Speed it up and the crests squeeze closer; make it heavier and the wave shrinks again, while a live readout and graph track the wavelength. We build lambda = h/mv step by step from momentum and the photon rule p = h/lambda, check the units, and compare an electron with a cricket ball. A worked example finds the wavelength of an electron at 3.0 x 10^6 m/s (2.42 x 10^-10 m, about the size of an atom) on a powers-of-ten ruler. Then electron diffraction rings and the electron microscope, the exam trap on units, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 19 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
